Public evidence: 313 stores in 99 cities at 31 March 2026, up from 237 a year earlier (76 opened in FY26)
Implication for the programme: A larger store estate can act as pickup, return and stock points for online orders.

Public evidence: 65.8 million Beauty orders in FY26 (+21%) from 19.7 million annual unique transacting customers
Implication for the programme: Even a small share of orders moved to collection is a large volume, so store processes must scale.

Public evidence: Fulfilment expense of ₹959 crore in FY26, 9.6% of revenue from operations (9.3% in FY25); it grew 29% against revenue growth of 26%
Implication for the programme: Collected orders and store returns avoid a last-mile trip or a reverse pickup; the pilot must measure how much this saves.

Public evidence: 5,879 consumer complaints received in FY26 against 6,933 in FY25, all closed
Implication for the programme: Complaints fell while orders grew. New journeys must not reverse this, so complaint handling is designed in from the start.

Public evidence: 31 warehouses and 37 rapid stores among 75 operating locations, alongside the retail stores
Implication for the programme: Stock sits in three kinds of location; online customers need one reliable view of store stock.

Public evidence: Main obligations of the DPDP Rules, 2025 apply from May 2027; e-commerce entities must acknowledge consumer complaints within 48 hours and resolve them within one month
Implication for the programme: Pickup codes, identity checks, notifications and refunds must comply from the first day of the pilot.
